title: What If the Colorado River Ran Dry?

scenes.text: What if the Colorado River ran dry? Almost 40 million people would feel it first.
Nearly 40 million people in seven states rely on the river for some or all of their city water.
It irrigates about 4.5 million acres of farmland, and the river already carries less than the amount promised from it.
The whole system stores about 60 million acre-feet, only about four years of the river's average flow.
So once the reservoirs ran low, cities and farms would face shortages within a few years, not decades.
Mexico gets a share too, 1.5 million acre-feet a year, so the shortage would not stop at the border.

description:
What if the Colorado River ran dry?
